report.incidentSummary: Starting at 14:35 UTC (20:05 IST) during the evening peak traffic window, the AI assistant experienced severe response latency (p95 jumping from ~7s to 24-26s) and elevated error rates (~4.5%). The issue was caused by requests exceeding the external llm-provider requests-per-minute (RPM) quota, resulting in HTTP 429 Too Many Requests responses. Assistant-orchestrator's retry backoffs added ~15-20 seconds per call, causing conversations to take 20-30 seconds and failing when retries were exhausted.
report.rootCauseStatement: During evening peak load, request traffic to the external llm-provider exceeded its configured requests-per-minute (RPM) quota limit. Assistant-orchestrator encountered repeated HTTP 429 Too Many Requests errors and initiated exponential backoff retries, driving orchestrator p95 latency to 24-26 seconds (dominated by llm_latency_p95_ms of 21-23 seconds) and triggering fallback answer failures when retry limits were exhausted.

hypotheses.cause: During evening peak traffic, assistant requests exceeded external llm-provider's requests-per-minute (RPM) quota, triggering HTTP 429 Too Many Requests responses and backoff retries in assistant-orchestrator that stretched total latency to 20-30 seconds and caused answer failures after exhausted retries.
hypotheses.rationale: Direct telemetry and logs show rate_limited_count surging to 22.5-60/min starting at 14:35 UTC, with assistant-orchestrator logging 72 instances of 'llm-provider returned 429 Too Many Requests (quota exceeded: requests per minute)' within 10 minutes. Upstream llm_latency_p95_ms jumped from 5.5s to 21-23s, fully accounting for the increase in total orchestrator p95 latency to 24-26s.

hypotheses.cause: Prompt template deployment CHG-48222 on assistant-orchestrator increased token lengths or processing time, replicating historical incident PIR-2007.
hypotheses.rationale: CHG-48222 was completed at 14:42 UTC, fully 7 minutes after orchestrator latency and 429 rate limit spikes had already started at 14:35 UTC. Furthermore, llm_tokens_per_min remained flat (~284k-338k tokens/min) throughout the incident, directly contradicting a prompt token inflation issue like PIR-2007.

facts.statement: assistant-orchestrator latency_p95_ms spiked from ~7,000 ms to 13,453 ms at 14:35 UTC and reached 24,140 ms at 14:40 UTC, remaining between 24,000 ms and 26,016 ms through 16:15 UTC.
assistant-orchestrator error_rate rose from ~0.5% to 1.79% at 14:35 UTC and remained elevated at 4.4% to 4.6% through 16:15 UTC.
assistant-orchestrator llm_latency_p95_ms increased from ~5,500 ms before 14:35 UTC to 10,650 ms at 14:35 UTC and peaked at 23,162 ms at 15:30 UTC.
assistant-orchestrator rate_limited_count jumped from ~0/min before 14:35 UTC to 22.54/min at 14:35 UTC and reached up to 59.94/min.

assistant-orchestrator logged 72 instances of 'llm-provider returned 429 Too Many Requests (quota exceeded: requests per minute)' between 14:35 UTC and 14:45 UTC, followed by conversation failures when retries were exhausted.
assistant-orchestrator llm_tokens_per_min remained flat between 284,296 and 337,704 tokens/min throughout the entire 13:45 to 16:15 UTC window.
CHG-48222 (prompt template update) was deployed to assistant-orchestrator at 14:42:00 UTC.
Downstream internal dependencies (cache, compliance-filter, knowledge-index, user-context-service) recorded zero ERROR/FATAL logs and maintained normal baseline p95 latencies throughout the window.
assistant-orchestrator connects to llm-provider with a 25,000 ms timeout and 2 retries.

inferences.statement: The 20-30 second response times experienced by users were caused by assistant-orchestrator executing multiple retry attempts with backoff against llm-provider after receiving HTTP 429 responses.
CHG-48222 is not the root cause because the incident onset (14:35 UTC) preceded its deployment completion (14:42 UTC) by 7 minutes, and token consumption metrics showed no surge.

All internal assistant dependencies (cache, user-context-service, knowledge-index, compliance-filter) operated within normal parameters and did not contribute to the latency spike or conversation errors.

assumptions.statement: The contractual requests-per-minute (RPM) quota allocated by llm-provider is inadequate for current peak evening assistant chat traffic volume.

timeline.event: assistant-orchestrator operating normally at ~7s p95 latency, ~0.5% error rate, and 0 rate-limited calls per minute.
Onset of incident: rate_limited_count spikes to 22.54/min as llm-provider emits HTTP 429 quota exceeded errors; orchestrator latency_p95 jumps to 13,453 ms and error_rate climbs to 1.79%.
Rate limiting escalates: rate_limited_count reaches 58.86/min, llm_latency_p95_ms reaches 20,985 ms, orchestrator latency_p95_ms reaches 24,140 ms, and error rate hits 4.43%.
CHG-48222 deployed to assistant-orchestrator (v0.42.0 -> v0.43.0, prompt template update); no change in token volume or error trajectory observed.
Peak latency observed with llm_latency_p95_ms reaching 23,162 ms and orchestrator latency_p95_ms reaching 26,016 ms.
Investigation window closes with latency and rate limiting persisting at high levels.

confidence.rationale: High confidence based on unambiguous metrics and log messages showing HTTP 429 quota exceeded errors from llm-provider coinciding exactly with the onset of latency spikes, while ruling out internal components and the prompt template release based on timing and stable token volume.

gaps.description: Direct incoming assistant request rate (QPS/RPM) metrics and external vendor account quota dashboard were not queried.
gaps.impact: Minimal impact; assistant-orchestrator rate_limited_count and log messages explicitly capture HTTP 429 'quota exceeded: requests per minute' responses from llm-provider.

recommendedActions.action: Request an immediate emergency quota increase for requests-per-minute (RPM) with llm-provider or configure a secondary fallback LLM provider.
recommendedActions.rationale: Peak evening traffic is exceeding the provisioned RPM quota limit at llm-provider, causing throttling and retries.
recommendedActions.verification: Confirm assistant-orchestrator rate_limited_count drops to 0/min during evening peak traffic.

recommendedActions.action: Tune assistant-orchestrator's retry and backoff parameters for HTTP 429 errors to avoid compounding delays that lead to 25s client-side timeouts.
recommendedActions.rationale: Executing multiple backoff retries against an already rate-limited provider stretches conversation latency to 20-26 seconds before failing.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify p95 latency under rate limit scenarios fails fast or responds within an acceptable degraded SLA threshold.

recommendedActions.action: Implement a client-side token bucket rate limiter and admission control at api-gateway or assistant-orchestrator for LLM queries.
recommendedActions.rationale: Smooths out sudden traffic bursts and prevents overwhelming the upstream vendor quota.
recommendedActions.verification: Monitor that outgoing RPM to llm-provider never breaches contractual rate limits.

report.justification: The investigation stopped completed without critic review, but the root cause is established conclusively by direct evidence. Metric rate_limited_count and error logs definitively identify HTTP 429 RPM quota exhaustion on llm-provider starting at 14:35 UTC, directly matching the 21-23s llm_latency_p95_ms and 24-26s total orchestrator p95 latency. Downstream internal dependencies were verified completely healthy, and the prompt deployment CHG-48222 was definitively ruled out as its completion (14:42 UTC) post-dates the onset by 7 minutes and token consumption was flat.

findings.summary: Assistant-orchestrator latency and error rate spiked starting at 14:35 UTC (20:05 IST), climbing to 24-26s p95 latency and ~4.5% error rate by 14:40 UTC. The 20-30s latency is directly driven by llm_latency_p95_ms (21-23s) and rate_limited_count (spiking to 40-60/min), with logs showing repeated HTTP 429 'quota exceeded: requests per minute' responses from llm-provider triggering retry backoffs. Token consumption (llm_tokens_per_min) remained flat (~320k tokens/min), confirming the issue is request-rate throttling rather than token explosion.

observations.statement: assistant-orchestrator latency_p95_ms spiked from a baseline of ~7,000 ms to 13,453 ms at 14:35 UTC and reached 24,140 ms at 14:40 UTC, remaining elevated between 24,000 ms and 26,016 ms throughout the remainder of the window. Error rate rose simultaneously from ~0.5% to 1.79% at 14:35 UTC and ~4.4%-4.6% from 14:40 UTC onwards.

assistant-orchestrator llm_latency_p95_ms increased from ~5,500 ms prior to 14:35 UTC to 10,650 ms at 14:35 UTC and 20,985 ms at 14:40 UTC, peaking at 23,162 ms at 15:30 UTC. This accounts for almost all of the orchestrator total p95 latency (~21-23s of the 24-26s total).
assistant-orchestrator llm_tokens_per_min remained steady between ~284,000 and 338,000 tokens/min throughout the entire 13:45-16:15 UTC window, showing no token volume explosion.

assistant-orchestrator rate_limited_count jumped from ~0/min to 22.54/min at 14:35 UTC and sustained between 39 and 60/min. Logs confirm frequent 'llm-provider returned 429 Too Many Requests (quota exceeded: requests per minute)' warnings with subsequent backoff retries, leading to exhausted retries and fallback errors.

The 20-30s total latency is caused by llm-provider rate-limiting (429 HTTP quota exceeded on requests per minute) and the resulting backoff retry loops within assistant-orchestrator, rather than a prompt token explosion or api-gateway timeout.

# Investigation report: Assistant very slow this evening

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** completed · **Confidence:** 0.95 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
Starting at 14:35 UTC (20:05 IST) during the evening peak traffic window, the AI assistant experienced severe response latency (p95 jumping from ~7s to 24-26s) and elevated error rates (~4.5%). The issue was caused by requests exceeding the external llm-provider requests-per-minute (RPM) quota, resulting in HTTP 429 Too Many Requests responses. Assistant-orchestrator's retry backoffs added ~15-20 seconds per call, causing conversations to take 20-30 seconds and failing when retries were exhausted.

**Root cause:** During evening peak load, request traffic to the external llm-provider exceeded its configured requests-per-minute (RPM) quota limit. Assistant-orchestrator encountered repeated HTTP 429 Too Many Requests errors and initiated exponential backoff retries, driving orchestrator p95 latency to 24-26 seconds (dominated by llm_latency_p95_ms of 21-23 seconds) and triggering fallback answer failures when retry limits were exhausted.

## Hypotheses
1. **During evening peak traffic, assistant requests exceeded external llm-provider's requests-per-minute (RPM) quota, triggering HTTP 429 Too Many Requests responses and backoff retries in assistant-orchestrator that stretched total latency to 20-30 seconds and caused answer failures after exhausted retries.** — `llm-provider`, rate_limiting_or_quota, confidence 0.95, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_2, ev_3, ev_5, ev_10, ev_16, ev_17] · Contradicting: none
   - Direct telemetry and logs show rate_limited_count surging to 22.5-60/min starting at 14:35 UTC, with assistant-orchestrator logging 72 instances of 'llm-provider returned 429 Too Many Requests (quota exceeded: requests per minute)' within 10 minutes. Upstream llm_latency_p95_ms jumped from 5.5s to 21-23s, fully accounting for the increase in total orchestrator p95 latency to 24-26s.
2. **Prompt template deployment CHG-48222 on assistant-orchestrator increased token lengths or processing time, replicating historical incident PIR-2007.** — `assistant-orchestrator`, deployment_regression, confidence 0.05, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_4, ev_8, ev_15, ev_18] · Contradicting: [ev_2, ev_4, ev_5, ev_10, ev_11, ev_16]
   - CHG-48222 was completed at 14:42 UTC, fully 7 minutes after orchestrator latency and 429 rate limit spikes had already started at 14:35 UTC. Furthermore, llm_tokens_per_min remained flat (~284k-338k tokens/min) throughout the incident, directly contradicting a prompt token inflation issue like PIR-2007.

## Facts
- assistant-orchestrator latency_p95_ms spiked from ~7,000 ms to 13,453 ms at 14:35 UTC and reached 24,140 ms at 14:40 UTC, remaining between 24,000 ms and 26,016 ms through 16:15 UTC. [ev_5]
- assistant-orchestrator error_rate rose from ~0.5% to 1.79% at 14:35 UTC and remained elevated at 4.4% to 4.6% through 16:15 UTC. [ev_3]
- assistant-orchestrator llm_latency_p95_ms increased from ~5,500 ms before 14:35 UTC to 10,650 ms at 14:35 UTC and peaked at 23,162 ms at 15:30 UTC. [ev_2]
- assistant-orchestrator rate_limited_count jumped from ~0/min before 14:35 UTC to 22.54/min at 14:35 UTC and reached up to 59.94/min. [ev_10]
- assistant-orchestrator logged 72 instances of 'llm-provider returned 429 Too Many Requests (quota exceeded: requests per minute)' between 14:35 UTC and 14:45 UTC, followed by conversation failures when retries were exhausted. [ev_16]
- assistant-orchestrator llm_tokens_per_min remained flat between 284,296 and 337,704 tokens/min throughout the entire 13:45 to 16:15 UTC window. [ev_11]
- CHG-48222 (prompt template update) was deployed to assistant-orchestrator at 14:42:00 UTC. [ev_4, ev_8]
- Downstream internal dependencies (cache, compliance-filter, knowledge-index, user-context-service) recorded zero ERROR/FATAL logs and maintained normal baseline p95 latencies throughout the window. [ev_1, ev_6, ev_7, ev_9, ev_12, ev_14]
- assistant-orchestrator connects to llm-provider with a 25,000 ms timeout and 2 retries. [ev_17]

## Inferences
- The 20-30 second response times experienced by users were caused by assistant-orchestrator executing multiple retry attempts with backoff against llm-provider after receiving HTTP 429 responses. [ev_2, ev_5, ev_10, ev_16, ev_17]
- CHG-48222 is not the root cause because the incident onset (14:35 UTC) preceded its deployment completion (14:42 UTC) by 7 minutes, and token consumption metrics showed no surge. [ev_4, ev_5, ev_10, ev_11]
- All internal assistant dependencies (cache, user-context-service, knowledge-index, compliance-filter) operated within normal parameters and did not contribute to the latency spike or conversation errors. [ev_1, ev_6, ev_7, ev_9, ev_12, ev_14]

## Assumptions
- The contractual requests-per-minute (RPM) quota allocated by llm-provider is inadequate for current peak evening assistant chat traffic volume.

## Timeline
- **2026-09-16T13:45:00.000Z (19:15 IST)** assistant-orchestrator operating normally at ~7s p95 latency, ~0.5% error rate, and 0 rate-limited calls per minute. [ev_2, ev_3, ev_5, ev_10]
- **2026-09-16T14:35:00.000Z (20:05 IST)** Onset of incident: rate_limited_count spikes to 22.54/min as llm-provider emits HTTP 429 quota exceeded errors; orchestrator latency_p95 jumps to 13,453 ms and error_rate climbs to 1.79%. [ev_3, ev_5, ev_10, ev_16]
- **2026-09-16T14:40:00.000Z (20:10 IST)** Rate limiting escalates: rate_limited_count reaches 58.86/min, llm_latency_p95_ms reaches 20,985 ms, orchestrator latency_p95_ms reaches 24,140 ms, and error rate hits 4.43%. [ev_2, ev_3, ev_5, ev_10, ev_16]
- **2026-09-16T14:42:00.000Z (20:12 IST)** CHG-48222 deployed to assistant-orchestrator (v0.42.0 -> v0.43.0, prompt template update); no change in token volume or error trajectory observed. [ev_4, ev_8, ev_11]
- **2026-09-16T15:30:00.000Z (21:00 IST)** Peak latency observed with llm_latency_p95_ms reaching 23,162 ms and orchestrator latency_p95_ms reaching 26,016 ms. [ev_2, ev_5]
- **2026-09-16T16:15:00.000Z (21:45 IST)** Investigation window closes with latency and rate limiting persisting at high levels. [ev_5, ev_10]

## Confidence
0.95: High confidence based on unambiguous metrics and log messages showing HTTP 429 quota exceeded errors from llm-provider coinciding exactly with the onset of latency spikes, while ruling out internal components and the prompt template release based on timing and stable token volume.

## Gaps
- Direct incoming assistant request rate (QPS/RPM) metrics and external vendor account quota dashboard were not queried. (impact: Minimal impact; assistant-orchestrator rate_limited_count and log messages explicitly capture HTTP 429 'quota exceeded: requests per minute' responses from llm-provider.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Request an immediate emergency quota increase for requests-per-minute (RPM) with llm-provider or configure a secondary fallback LLM provider. [ev_10, ev_16]
  - Why: Peak evening traffic is exceeding the provisioned RPM quota limit at llm-provider, causing throttling and retries.
  - Verify: Confirm assistant-orchestrator rate_limited_count drops to 0/min during evening peak traffic.
- **[next]** Tune assistant-orchestrator's retry and backoff parameters for HTTP 429 errors to avoid compounding delays that lead to 25s client-side timeouts. [ev_2, ev_5, ev_16, ev_17]
  - Why: Executing multiple backoff retries against an already rate-limited provider stretches conversation latency to 20-26 seconds before failing.
  - Verify: Verify p95 latency under rate limit scenarios fails fast or responds within an acceptable degraded SLA threshold.
- **[later]** Implement a client-side token bucket rate limiter and admission control at api-gateway or assistant-orchestrator for LLM queries. [ev_10, ev_17]
  - Why: Smooths out sudden traffic bursts and prevents overwhelming the upstream vendor quota.
  - Verify: Monitor that outgoing RPM to llm-provider never breaches contractual rate limits.

## Justification
The investigation stopped completed without critic review, but the root cause is established conclusively by direct evidence. Metric rate_limited_count and error logs definitively identify HTTP 429 RPM quota exhaustion on llm-provider starting at 14:35 UTC, directly matching the 21-23s llm_latency_p95_ms and 24-26s total orchestrator p95 latency.
